title: Successive ionisation energies of aluminium
caption: On a log scale each ionisation is a little harder than the last, with two large jumps: after the 3rd electron (the next comes from the second shell) and after the 11th (the next comes from the first). Three outer electrons put aluminium in group 13.
alt: Line graph of the 13 successive ionisation energies of aluminium on a logarithmic axis, rising gradually with big jumps between the 3rd and 4th and between the 11th and 12th.
description: Ionisations 1 to 3: 578, 1817 and 2745 kJ mol⁻¹, the three outer electrons.
Ionisation 4 jumps to 11 577 kJ mol⁻¹: the electron comes from the second shell.
Ionisations 4 to 11 rise steadily to 42 647; ionisations 12 and 13 jump to about 201 000 and 222 000, the first shell.
